description: Long Beach, California-based vertically integrated space and defense company. Operates two primary business lines: Launch Services (Electron small-sat rocket, HASTE hypersonic test vehicle) and Space Systems (satellite design and manufacture, spacecraft components including solar panels, reaction wheels, star trackers, and radios). Electron, the world's most frequently launched privately-developed small rocket, completed 21 missions in 2025 with a 100% success rate. Developing Neutron, a partially reusable medium-lift rocket targeted for first launch in Q4 2026 or early 2027.
key_facts: Full Year 2025 revenue: $602M (+38% YoY); Q4 2025 revenue: $180M (record); GAAP gross margin Q4: 37.9%
Record backlog: $1.85B at end-2025 (+73% YoY); cash position $829M (from $271M in 2024)
Net loss FY2025: $198M; company profitable at gross margin level but not yet at operating income level
Q1 2026 guidance: $185–200M revenue (+57% YoY); non-GAAP gross margin 39–41%; adj. EBITDA loss $21–27M
December 2025: $816M SDA contract to build 18 satellites for Tracking Layer Tranche 3 missile-warning constellation — largest ever single contract
HASTE hypersonic test program: $190M block-buy for 20 suborbital flights under MACH-TB 2.0; also onramped to multi-billion NSSL Phase 3 launch services pool

Neutron development: first launch targeted Q4 2026 after Stage 1 tank rupture during qualification (manufacturing defect in hand-laid autoclave joint); ~$360M cumulative program spend through end-2025
Archimedes engine (methane/LOx, 1.5M lbf aggregate thrust on Neutron first stage) testing 20 hrs/day, 7 days/week at NASA Stennis
21 Electron launches in 2025 — 100% mission success rate; cumulative Electron launch count exceeded 70
52-week range: $20.23–$99.58; all-time closing high $96.30 on January 16, 2026
200-day MA ~$68; 50-day MA ~$72 (as of early May 2026) — stock trading above both
Analyst consensus: 9 Buy, 5 Hold, 1 Sell (17 analysts); mean price target ~$83

blurb: Rocket Lab Corporation is a Long Beach, California-based vertically integrated space and defense company. It operates two primary business lines: Launch Services (Electron small-sat rocket, HASTE hypersonic test vehicle) and Space Systems (satellite design and manufacture, spacecraft components including solar panels, reaction wheels, star trackers, and radios). Electron, the world's most frequently launched privately-developed small rocket, completed 21 missions in 2025 with a 100% success rate. The company is developing Neutron, a partially reusable medium-lift rocket targeted for first launch in Q4 2026 or early 2027.
recent: Full-year 2025 revenue was $602 million (+38% YoY) on a record $1.85 billion backlog (+73% YoY), with a $198 million net loss; Q1 2026 guidance calls for $185–200 million revenue (+57% YoY). In December 2025 Rocket Lab won an $816 million SDA contract to build 18 satellites for the Tracking Layer Tranche 3 missile-warning constellation — its largest ever single contract — and the HASTE hypersonic test program now carries a $190 million block-buy for 20 suborbital flights under MACH-TB 2.0. Neutron development continues at NASA Stennis after a Stage 1 tank rupture during qualification was traced to a manufacturing defect; cumulative program spend is approximately $360 million through end-2025. The stock closed near $78 in early May 2026 against a 52-week range of $20.23–$99.58.
